subject: physics
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: As an object moves in uniform circular motion, which quantity remains constant?
questions.explain: Speed is constant, but velocity, acceleration and momentum continuously change direction.

questions.q: For a simple pendulum of length L, the period of small oscillations is:
questions.explain: The simple pendulum period is T = 2π√(L/g).

questions.q: An angle of 1 radian corresponds to an arc length equal to:
questions.explain: One radian subtends an arc length equal to the radius.

questions.q: For circular motion, which expression for centripetal acceleration uses angular speed ω?
questions.explain: Since v = ωr, the acceleration v²/r equals ω²r.

questions.q: The period of a simple pendulum depends on:
questions.explain: For small angles the period depends only on length L and gravitational field strength g.

questions.q: In SHM, the maximum speed of an oscillator of amplitude A is:
questions.explain: Maximum speed v_max = ωA, occurring at the equilibrium position.

questions.q: At the equilibrium position in SHM, the energy is:
questions.explain: At equilibrium displacement is zero so PE is minimum and KE is maximum.

questions.q: The total energy of a mass m in SHM with amplitude A and angular frequency ω is:
questions.explain: Total energy E = ½mω²A², equal to the maximum kinetic energy ½m(ωA)².

questions.q: The angular speed ω of an object completing one revolution in period T is:
questions.explain: One revolution is 2π radians, so ω = 2π/T.

questions.q: In SHM, the acceleration is always directed:
questions.explain: The restoring acceleration always points back toward the equilibrium position.

questions.q: The defining equation for simple harmonic motion is:
questions.explain: In SHM, acceleration is proportional to displacement and directed opposite to it: a = −ω²x.

questions.q: The relationship between linear speed v and angular speed ω for radius r is:
questions.explain: Linear speed v = ωr.

questions.q: For a mass m on a spring of stiffness k, the period of SHM is:
questions.explain: The period of a mass–spring oscillator is T = 2π√(m/k).

questions.q: A car rounds a flat curve. The force providing the centripetal force is:
questions.explain: On a flat road, friction between the tyres and road supplies the centripetal force.

questions.q: A free oscillation occurs when a system oscillates at its:
options: Natural frequency with no external periodic force
questions.explain: Free oscillations occur at the natural frequency with no external driving force.

questions.q: In SHM, the phase difference between displacement and acceleration is:
questions.explain: Acceleration is exactly out of phase (π rad) with displacement, since a = −ω²x.

questions.q: For an object in uniform circular motion, the net (resultant) force is:
questions.explain: The resultant (centripetal) force points toward the centre of the circle.

questions.q: Increasing the degree of damping on a resonating system causes the resonance peak to:
questions.explain: Greater damping lowers and broadens the resonance peak (and slightly lowers its frequency).

questions.q: A 0.50 kg ball moves in a horizontal circle of radius 2.0 m at 4.0 m s⁻¹. The centripetal force is:
At the point of maximum displacement in SHM, the oscillator has:
questions.explain: At the extremes velocity is zero and acceleration (restoring force) is maximum.

questions.q: The velocity in SHM as a function of displacement x is v = ±ω√(A²−x²). At equilibrium (x=0), the speed is:
questions.explain: At x = 0 the speed is maximum, equal to ωA.

questions.q: An object moves in a circle of radius r at constant speed v. Its centripetal acceleration is given by:
questions.explain: Centripetal acceleration is a = v²/r, directed toward the centre.

questions.q: Why does the centripetal force do no work on an object in uniform circular motion?
options: Speed is constant so energy is conserved automatically
The force is perpendicular to the velocity
questions.explain: The centripetal force points toward the centre, perpendicular to the velocity, so it does no work.

questions.q: Light damping causes the amplitude of free oscillations to:
questions.explain: With light damping the amplitude decays exponentially while oscillation continues.

questions.q: A heavily (over) damped system, when displaced and released:
options: Returns to equilibrium very slowly without oscillating
questions.explain: Heavy damping causes a slow return to equilibrium with no oscillation.

questions.q: Resonance occurs when the driving frequency equals the system's:
questions.explain: Resonance gives maximum amplitude when the driving frequency matches the natural frequency.

questions.q: In SHM, the maximum acceleration of an oscillator of amplitude A is:
questions.explain: Maximum acceleration a_max = ω²A, occurring at maximum displacement.

questions.q: In SHM, the phase difference between displacement and velocity is:
questions.explain: Velocity leads displacement by π/2 (a quarter cycle) in SHM.

questions.q: For SHM described by x = A cos(ωt), the velocity is given by:
questions.explain: Differentiating x = A cos(ωt) gives v = −Aω sin(ωt).

questions.q: During SHM, total mechanical energy (in the absence of damping):
options: Stays constant as KE and PE interchange
questions.explain: Total energy is constant; kinetic and potential energy interchange throughout the cycle.
